interest: For historians studying the prelude to the Pacific War, this document illustrates the State Department's decimal indexing and cross-referencing system regarding Japanese military expansion into Southeast Asia. It demonstrates how U.S. diplomats in Chungking and Tokyo gathered and cross-checked intelligence from Chinese Foreign Office and British diplomatic channels in May and July 1941 concerning Japanese ultimatums for naval and air bases in southern Indochina (Saigon). It also provides direct archival citations to the primary State Department decimal classifications where the full substantive telegrams were filed.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46, dated October 12, 1945) cataloging records under decimal file 894.34551G relating to Japanese naval and coaling stations and air/naval bases in French Indochina during mid-1941. The sheet records two cross-referenced telegrams: Sub. No. 2 of May 9, 1941, from U.S. Ambassador Nelson T. Johnson in Chungking relaying Chinese intelligence on Japanese demands for air and naval bases and troop landings at Saigon (cross-referenced to 751g.94/244); and Sub. No. 3 of July 16, 1941, from U.S. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo transmitting British diplomatic information regarding Japanese demands on France for bases in French Indochina (cross-referenced to 740.0011 E.W. 1929/257).

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers cataloging cross-referenced documents regarding Japanese demands for naval and air bases in French Indochina in 1941.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State List of Papers sheet (Form DS-46), dated October 12, 1945, indexes documents categorized under decimal file 894.34551G regarding Japanese naval bases in French Indochina. It indexes two telegrams from 1941: one from Ambassador Nelson T. Johnson in Chungking reporting Chinese intelligence on Japanese demands for bases and troop landings at Saigon, and one from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo relaying British reports on Japanese demands upon France. Both items direct researchers to the primary decimal classifications where the telegrams were filed (751g.94/244 and 740.0011 E.W. 1929/257).
